parentRequirement: User complete pluggable system and cross-lead unique take; Mika X01-06 Settings runtime management request

findings.fact: PluginManagement is lazy via open=false return and keyed by sessionId plus project scope. It consumes a narrow read-only registry and separate local Browser extensions source. App constructs the current registry reader; adding real commands requires an explicit host port and App integration scope, currently overlapping Recovery ownership.
findings.implication: An isolated component can be prepared after legal supply/take; final App wiring must wait for the existing owner handoff, never claim the old released X03 scope.

findings.topic: Mutation is not a read retry
findings.fact: useRead aborts outdated reads and retries by incrementing attempt; it is not a command authority.
findings.implication: Use one private per-session/install command state machine: freeze validated request and idempotency key before await; single flight; explicit identical retry only; typed409 keeps the editable draft; aborted/disconnected/malformed or mismatched ACK remains UNKNOWN. New read of current state cannot prove the historical command never happened.

findings.fact: Fixed main client has generic commandPlugin transport and no implemented owner pluginRuntime/commandPluginRuntime methods in these source inputs. Mika reports those methods as the current independent X01-CLI-COMMANDS01 interface being implemented, not an already reviewed main consumer dependency.
findings.implication: Wait for exact source/helper delivery and reuse its runtime decoding. Do not add a second fetch transport or cast a mutation response into success. Config/grant editing needs its acknowledged shared decoder before inclusion.

findings.topic: Material identity and first enable target
findings.fact: PluginMaterialInstall contains registrationId/versionId/admittedRevision, material operation ID, storeId, status and material/tree digests, but no targetRunnerId. Runtime view includes targetRunnerId only for an enabled binding; disabled coherent state has null target/store/material identities. Enable command requires an explicit targetRunnerId/storeId/materialInstallOperationId. The examined runtime route module exposes runner publication and runtime/binding reads, but no owner host-directory endpoint.
findings.implication: Future owner must resolve the first-enable host selection interface with db owner. Do not infer a runner from an installed-material receipt, an ordinary runner status, or the current disabled runtime. A known prior binding can support presentation but is not fresh capability permission. If manual exact identity entry is intentionally chosen, label it and let the existing server validate; never fabricate a loaded/ready host.

findings.fact: Runtime contract distinguishes desiredEnabled, bindingAllowed/reason, enabled/current revision and exact install/runner/store identity, while loaded and callable are literal unknown. Material installed is a static receipt.
findings.implication: Show these separately, map reasons into actionable plain language, keep Browser extensions local state independent. A successful enable allows new tool-task binding; it does not prove package execution or cancel already-running tasks.

candidateAcceptance: No command before an explicit user action; immutable body/key for identical retry.
Changes to session, installation or project isolate late ACKs and cancel local pending work without claiming server cancellation.
409 preserves inputs and exposes current revision; uncertain ACK keeps recovery action distinct from refresh.
First-enable target is supplied by an agreed public interface or an explicit reviewed input path, not inferred from material.
Light/dark, narrow layout, keyboard focus and disabled/pending/unknown states remain legible; no automatic retry on mount or refresh.
ownership: No new worktree, task, claim or feature write. Manager queues as NOT_TAKEN behind Release safe point; exact literal scopes and registry authority must be settled before implementation.

method.application: Reuse installed skills already read in this task; inspect existing module responsibility and public typed contracts, preserve a deep command boundary, avoid duplicating state/transport.
